claims.text: Pulumi maintains a documented provider support policy that specifies how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
Some Pulumi providers receive long-term security updates while others do not.
Pulumi publishes a 'Provider support policy' page at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/.
Pulumi does not automatically rollback changes made during an update if an error or failure occurs.
When an error or failure occurs during a Pulumi update, Pulumi completes any pending operations currently in progress and then exits and reports the error or failure.

To accomplish a manual rollback after a failed Pulumi deployment, you revert the code and configuration changes of the failed deployment and run `pulumi up` to update your infrastructure to its previous state.
Pulumi does not automatically query your cloud provider's live state before running `pulumi up` or `pulumi preview`.
Pulumi compares the desired state declared in your program against the last recorded state to determine what changes to make.
Refreshing state requires a round-trip to the cloud provider for every resource in a stack, which adds significant latency, especially for large stacks.
Running `pulumi refresh` synchronizes Pulumi's recorded state with the actual state of your cloud resources.
You can refresh and apply your desired state in a single step using `pulumi up --refresh`.
Pulumi Cloud provides built-in drift detection for automated drift detection and remediation on a schedule.
Pulumi resources have different logical names and physical names.
A Pulumi resource's logical name is part of the auto-assigned resource URN.
A Pulumi resource's logical name only needs to be unique within a stack.
A Pulumi resource's physical name typically needs to be unique within a certain scope, sometimes even globally.
Pulumi automatically creates each resource's physical name by combining the logical name with a random suffix appended afterwards.
Pulumi's auto-naming approach allows Pulumi to replace resources with less downtime, by creating the replacement before needing to delete the old resource.
A Pulumi resource's auto-named physical name will typically look like `my-bucket-d7c2fa0` instead of `my-bucket`.
You can disable Pulumi's resource auto-naming on a per-resource basis.
You can use project or stack configuration to customize or disable Pulumi's auto-naming globally, per provider, or per resource type.
Pulumi provides primitives so secrets are stored in a secure manner in the CLI, state file, and Pulumi Cloud.
During a Pulumi update, secrets are decrypted in memory and visible to the Pulumi program.
You may pass `--secret` to `pulumi config set` to cause a configuration value to be encrypted so it can be safely persisted in `Pulumi.<stack-name>.yaml`.
For every stack, Pulumi Cloud manages a unique encryption key, which it uses to encrypt secrets for that stack.
Pulumi Cloud's per-stack encryption key is configurable to use your own custom secrets provider.

Because a different encryption key is used for each stack, encrypting the same value across two different stacks leads to different encrypted strings being stored in the `Pulumi.<stack-name>.yaml` files.
You cannot copy an encrypted value from one `Pulumi.<stack-name>.yaml` file to another using a text editor; instead you must use `pulumi config set`.
When you run a preview, update, or destroy, Pulumi decrypts secret configuration data.
Secret data is plain text during the execution of a Pulumi deployment, and any part of the Pulumi program may access it using the Pulumi config object.
Pulumi does not use the Terraform engine in any way.
Some Pulumi providers use the open-source Terraform schemas in order to know what resources and parameters are available, and to determine the return and response attributes.
Pulumi native providers are mapped directly to the cloud provider APIs and do not use Terraform schemas.
Pulumi is a declarative tool that uses imperative languages to define your end state.
Pulumi's programming language is used for authoring your program and is not used for talking to the cloud provider API.
Pulumi uses strongly typed languages with programming languages that support IntelliSense and the Language Server Protocol.
Some Pulumi functionality is released as experimental.
Pulumi experimental features are always opt-in: they are enabled explicitly with a flag, command, or environment variable such as `PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true`.
Pulumi experimental features are not necessarily supported and can change or be removed at any time without a deprecation cycle.
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers Pulumi maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The provider support policy page lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older major versions of Pulumi providers receive no patches at all.
You can find the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi in the Pulumi Registry.
When a major version of a provider is released, that is a signal to begin planning a provider version update.
Major provider versions typically include significant changes such as deprecations, new resources, and new functionality, which may require additional migration steps.
Pulumi recommends that, at least quarterly, you consider updating to the latest minor version on the current major and minimally review provider release notes.
Minor provider versions typically include new resources and features, performance improvements, and bug fixes without introducing breaking changes.
Pulumi recommends always allowing patch updates on the current minor, for example using the tilde operator in npm such as ~1.2.3.
Patch versions of Pulumi providers are primarily for bug fixes and security updates and are designed to be fully backward compatible.
Pulumi recommends never being 2 major versions behind on a provider, as it is inadvisable to jump a major version due to the number of potential breaking changes across the major versions.

Each major version of a Pulumi provider includes migration logic to smooth the upgrade from the immediately previous major version, but these migrations do not always work across multiple major versions.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault are the current list of providers that receive long-term support updates on eligible older versions.
The Pulumi AWS provider registry page is located at /registry/packages/aws/.
The Pulumi Azure Classic provider registry page is located at /registry/packages/azure/.
The Pulumi Azure Native provider registry page is located at /registry/packages/azure-native/.
The Pulumi Azure AD provider registry page is located at /registry/packages/azuread/.
The Pulumi Command provider registry page is located at /registry/packages/command/.
The Pulumi Docker Build provider registry page is located at /registry/packages/docker-build/.
The Pulumi GCP provider registry page is located at /registry/packages/gcp/.
The Pulumi Kubernetes provider registry page is located at /registry/packages/kubernetes/.
The Pulumi TLS provider registry page is located at /registry/packages/tls/.
The Pulumi Vault provider registry page is located at /registry/packages/vault/.
The Pulumi provider long-term support (LTS) branch ships fixes for CVEs affecting the provider's code or its direct dependencies.
The Pulumi provider LTS branch ships fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship CVE security patches.
A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions.
A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain new resources or new resource properties.
A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain performance improvements.
A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain non-security bug fixes.
A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain compatibility updates for newer versions of language runtimes.
Pulumi providers will be compatible with the version of Pulumi they were frozen at unless otherwise prompted via security fixes.
Exactly one long-term support major version exists per Pulumi provider at any time.
When major version N+1 of a Pulumi provider ships, N+1 becomes the new current major (N), and the old current major (N) becomes the new long-term support major.

When a Pulumi provider's long-term support major is superseded, the old long-term support major reaches end of life on the same day the new major ships, regardless of how much of its 12-month support window remained.
Within a Pulumi provider's long-term support major version, only the latest minor version receives patches, and earlier minors are frozen.
Pulumi provider LTS releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases, but are tagged differently.
Pulumi recommends that customers pin to a specific major provider version.
Customers who pin a Pulumi provider to a specific major version automatically receive patch releases as they ship.
At any time, exactly one major version of a covered Pulumi provider is the LTS version.
Older major versions of a covered Pulumi provider (older than the LTS major) receive no patches.
The current major provider version (N) is supported until N+1 ships and receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions.
The long-term support provider version (N−1) is supported for up to 12 months from N's release, or until N+1 ships, and receives security updates in the provider's code or its direct dependencies.
Provider versions at N−2 and older are end of life, are not supported, and will not receive updates.
The 'Best practices for maintaining provider versions' guidance is located at /docs/support/faq/infrastructure/#what-are-the-best-practices-for-maintaining-provider-versions.
The Pulumi Registry is located at /registry/.
The 'Getting support' page is located at /docs/support/getting-support/.
